name: IndiaMART InterMESH Ltd
title: IndiaMART InterMESH Ltd - 542726 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Paying suppliers fell 1,200 in Q4 as Silver churn rose to ~7% monthly and gross adds slowed; growth now rests almost entirely on ARPU (8-9%) with customer growth only 1-2%.

summary.headline: IndiaMART Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14% YoY to Rs 404 crore, but paying suppliers fell 1,200 QoQ amid pricing pressure and elevated Silver churn.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 14% YoY to Rs 404 crore in Q4 and 13% to Rs 1,569 crore for FY26, with consolidated EBITDA of Rs 133 crore (33% margin) in Q4. Net profit fell to Rs 50 crore in Q4 because of a Rs 34 crore mark-to-market loss on treasury bonds, versus Rs 475 crore for the full year. Paying suppliers rose 3,200 in FY26 to 2.2 lakh but declined 1,200 in Q4, which management attributes to a Silver tier price increase at the end of Q2 and the war that broke out in late February. Management gave no net-add guidance and said it is not reversing pricing.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 133 crore (33% margin) / Rs 530 crore (34% margin)
Negative Rs 34 crore, driven by treasury mark-to-market losses

segments.name: IndiaMART standalone
segments.commentary: Collections from customers were Rs 546 crore in Q4 (+8% YoY) and Rs 1,674 crore in FY26 (+10% YoY).

segments.name: Busy Infotech
segments.commentary: Q4 billing was Rs 45 crore and FY26 billing Rs 170 crore; normalised growth excluding the payout structure change was 24% in Q4 and 43% for the year. Q4 revenue was Rs 34 crore (+53% normalised) and FY26 revenue Rs 119 crore (+44% normalised); deferred revenue was Rs 124 crore (+44% normalised).

segments.name: Export business
segments.commentary: Management said export collections are now Rs 60-70 crore, versus Rs 50-60 crore earlier and Rs 20-25 crore when the business was purely domestic.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for double-digit growth in the near term, driven by ARPU growth of about 8-9% and paying-supplier growth of about 1-2%.
No guidance on net adds until multiple quarters of sustained improvement; management said churn must improve before gross adds can translate into net adds.
Management said it will not roll back pricing, and expects gross adds to normalise only slowly.
Dividend of Rs 60 per share declared (final Rs 30 plus special Rs 30), subject to shareholder approval; management will revisit the payout approach next year.
Management said Platinum and Gold customers are about 50% of the customer base and more than 75% of revenue.
capex_capacity: No capex figure, capacity metric or commissioning timeline was disclosed on the call; the discussion covered platform and product levers rather than capital spending.

Busy Infotech: 11 thousand new licences sold in Q4 and about 45 thousand in FY26, taking the total licence count to 4 lakh 42 thousand; AI-led features are being added to the Busy product, with no timeline given.
Platform headroom: management sees about 2x supplier headroom over the current 0.25 million paying base, and says about 80% of buyer product and location needs are already met on the platform.
Headcount is 6,200 with no planned rationalisation; campus hiring continues periodically to scale servicing and sales teams, and management said current staffing is at the required level.
demand_pricing: Unique business enquiries were about 27 million in Q4 and declined about 1% YoY; management attributed the drag to added buyer verification, which it estimated cuts traffic-to-enquiry conversion by about 1%.

Paying suppliers were 2.2 lakh at FY26 end; Q4 decline of 1,200 was attributed to a Silver price increase at the end of Q2 and the war that started in late February. Management estimated the war cost about 1,000-1,500 gross adds and pricing about 1,000-1,500.
Silver churn is elevated: about 7% monthly and about 4% annual, versus 5-6% monthly previously. Platinum churn is well under 1% a month, and Gold is 1-1.5% a month.
Registered buyers rose 9% YoY while active buyers fell 3% YoY, which management linked to agentic and bot traffic and new OTP verification.
Management said price increases apply only to new subscribers, so ARPU uplift is gradual over 1-3 years; revenue is recognised on an 18-month moving average.
Management said about 80% of buyer product and location needs are already met on the platform, and sees a 2x supplier headroom versus the current 0.25 million paying base.

qa_highlights.question: When will gross adds recover to support a net-add trajectory of 5-6% annually, and how much of the weakness is due to the war versus pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no net-add guidance. It estimated the Q4 shortfall at roughly 3,000 customers versus a positive trend, split between the war and the price increase, and said February-March normally perform better.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a vicious-cycle risk given flat or declining enquiries and buyers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged the risk and described the business as at a plateau on an S-curve, needing a new product-market-fit lever to lift buyer frequency and supplier retention.

qa_highlights.question: Is ARPU growth going to be the main growth driver, and what are the VAS and credit options?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to rely only on ARPU, with customer and ARPU growth both needed until supplier count nears 4-5 lakh. Export is Rs 60-70 crore and logistics and credit are still pilots.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ARPU flat despite price hikes, and why did employee expenses decline QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Price hikes apply only to new subscribers and roll out over 1-3 years, and revenue uses an 18-month moving average. The Q4 employee expense decline reflected a Rs 8.5 crore labour code charge taken in Q3; headcount is 6,200 with no planned rationalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise payout or move to buybacks given cash generation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 40-60% of cash generated has been distributed over the last three to four years, and the Board chose a Rs 60 dividend, with a re-evaluation next year. Buybacks were deemed no different from dividends for now.

risks_watch: Elevated Silver churn (about 7% monthly) and slow gross-add recovery, with no net-add guidance.
Enquiry growth has stalled at 27-28 million per quarter despite performance marketing, and buyer verification may reduce conversion further.
Traffic and discovery risk from AI and chat platforms, though management said B2B enquiries are not yet declining.
Treasury mark-to-market losses from rising bond yields, which hit Q4 other income by Rs 34 crore.
Busy Infotech's normalised growth depends on the payout structure change; watch the Busy billing trend and AI feature rollout.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term platform and cash position, but cautious and somewhat defensive on the near-term supplier and buyer trends. Management attributed weakness mainly to the war and pricing, did not commit to a recovery timeline, and avoided giving numerical net-add or traffic guidance.
key_quotes: So we'll continue to have no guidance on the net adds until we have multiple quarters of continual success.
But we are not going back on pricing.
Currently, since the customer growth is hardly 1 - 2%, so most of the growth is coming from ARPU which is growing at 8 - 9%.
Yes, there is definitely a worry of falling into the vicious loop because that virtuous cycle where the suppliers were increasing and buyers were increasing.

growth.why: Management aims for double-digit near-term growth from ARPU growth of about 8-9% and paying-supplier growth of about 1-2%, but gives no net-add guidance and paying suppliers fell 1,200 in Q4; backing is pricing-led with no capacity or order numbers.
